en: Jose Rizal wrote the novels Noli Me Tangere and El Filibusterismo to expose Spanish colonial abuses in the Philippines.
The Philippine eagle, scientifically named Pithecophaga jefferyi, is the national bird of the Philippines and is critically endangered.
Indigenous Ifugao ancestors carved the Banaue Rice Terraces into the mountains over two thousand years ago for agriculture.
Emilio Aguinaldo proclaimed Philippine independence from Spain on June 12, 1898, at his ancestral home in Kawit, Cavite.
The Supreme Court heads the judicial branch of the Philippine government and interprets the constitutionality of laws.
Pediatrician Dr. Fe del Mundo invented a bamboo incubator to help care for premature babies in rural areas.
The Sinulog Festival in Cebu honors the Santo Niño with a traditional two-steps-forward, one-step-backward dance every January.
The T'boli people of South Cotabato weave T'nalak cloth from abaca fibers using traditional, dream-inspired patterns.
Filipino painter Juan Luna won a gold medal in Madrid in 1884 for his famous masterpiece Spoliarium.
Baybayin is an ancient Philippine writing system where each character represents a complete syllable rather than a single letter.
Intramuros is the historic walled area in Manila that served as the seat of the Spanish colonial government.
Gabriela Silang led an Ilocano revolt against Spanish colonial abuses after her husband Diego Silang was assassinated in 1763.
